claim_audit_results.claim_summary: Ten-row risk register R01-R10 with likelihood, impact and mitigation covering research and administrative risks.
Risk philosophy: prospective performance loss treated as a quantified scientific result with limited transparent recalibration rather than hidden.
Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route is a contingency for loss of primary farmer-site access (R04, task T3.6).
Project Steering Group meets at M6, M14, M18, M24, M27 issuing go/no-go verdicts on MS1-MS5, with M27 a mid-placement review; CDP reviewed at the same points.
Career Development Plan is deliverable D1.3, due M3, reviewed at each steering point.
HUN-REN ATK is the sole beneficiary, recruiting organisation and academic host at Martonvásár, hosting the fellow in its Agricultural Institute.
Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is the recruited experienced researcher/postdoctoral fellow.
Dr. Roland Hollós, research associate (Dept of Crop Production) and HUN-REN AI Ambassador (ORCID 0000-0001-5137-7471), is primary supervisor providing the modelling/data-integration environment.
The host provides in-house computational/data-processing environment with escalation to wider HUN-REN infrastructure.
Plant Physiology and Metabolomics Department led by Prof. Tibor Janda supplies complementary drought/abiotic-stress physiology depth.
HUN-REN ATK previously hosted and coordinated the funded MSCA Individual Fellowship LANDRACES (H2020 752453, MSCA-IF-EF-ST, 2017-2019).
Supervisor's modelling line (Hollós et al. 2026) and ATK's CORDIS-verified Horizon participations (COUSIN, AI4SoilHealth, TUdi) document research standing.
As a research organisation, ATK routes teaching/outreach through guest sessions at MATE and the Agricultural University of Plovdiv rather than in-house degree teaching.
ATK acts as recruiting organisation and beneficiary, providing workspace, integration, administrative support and continuation of arrangements during the M25-M30 placement.

claim_audit_results.claim_summary: FIELDWISE is a European Fellowship (intra-EU Bulgaria-to-Hungary) with the six-month placement as a CC-07 extension; the Global Fellowship outgoing/return-host requirement does not apply.
The inter-sectoral placement runs M25-M30 as the mobility element of the European Fellowship.

AgroVIR provides structured requirements consultation from M1 through WP4 and the real farm-management environment for MVP operational evaluation during the placement.
AgroVIR has no EU-funded research participation; FMIS in production across >745,000 ha in eight countries incl. Hungary and Bulgaria.

claim_audit_results.claim_summary: MATE (Institute of Horticultural Sciences) is the source scientific environment providing the 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive, plant material, trials, irrigation treatments and agronomic knowledge.

MATE's validation instrument base includes TDR/capacitive soil-moisture sensors at 15/30 cm, stomatal resistance/conductance equipment, SPAD meters, VIS-NIR (~325-1075 nm) and VIS-NIR-SWIR (~350-2500 nm) spectroradiometers, meteorology, leaf-temperature and CWSI tools.
Prof. Gábor Milics provides precision-agriculture depth at MATE.
MATE project contact is Dr. Sándor Takács.
